bull.t: Improved balance sheet and lower leverage
bull.b: Substantial debt reduction and positive equity provide a stronger capitalization base than in 2024. This lowers financial leverage and may improve flexibility as the company funds research, although ongoing losses continue to consume assets.

Adding a director with deep genomics, immune-response and biomedical research experience can improve oversight of the fibroblast-based pipeline. Stronger scientific governance may support better research prioritization and translation toward clinical applications.

The financing supplies immediate working capital for general corporate purposes and pipeline advancement, extending operating capacity in a pre-commercial business. It also provides potential additional proceeds if warrants are exercised, supporting near-term funding flexibility.

bear.b: A lack of revenue means the company has no commercial cash-generating engine to offset research and operating costs. Persistently large losses, after rising from about $5.1M in 2022, indicate substantial dependence on future financing or successful product development.

bear.t: Persistent cash burn and external funding dependence
bear.b: Ongoing negative operating and free cash flow steadily consumes the balance sheet and limits financial independence. With no revenue base, the company likely needs additional capital to sustain operations, creating financing, dilution and execution risks.

Potential loss of Nasdaq listing could reduce access to institutional investors, impair trading liquidity and complicate future capital raising. The company stated there is no assurance its appeal will succeed, leaving a material structural risk to financing and market access.
